page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.26xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture and deployed through the KVM hypervisor. The instance provides 104 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. Backing these processing threads is 768.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.38 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is not equipped with local storage and includes zero graphics acceleration hardware.

Network performance is sustained by a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. Because local physical storage is absent, all system drives and persistence layers must be mounted via remote network-attached cloud disks. Additionally, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned to the virtual machine by default, requiring network routing or elastic IP allocation for public-facing communication.

The dense RAM capacity paired with 104 dedicated cores offers favorable qualitative cost efficiency for architectures limited by memory capacity rather than raw compute cycles. The reliance on remote volumes represents an I/O tradeoff, making external throughput and storage tiering critical operational considerations. This configuration is aligned with large-scale in-memory databases, Redis or Memcached distributed caching layers, enterprise resource planning platforms, and big data in-memory processing frameworks.

The significant memory density coupled with 104 processing threads delivers efficient resource utilization for memory-heavy computing tasks.
